mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (exceeding 0.5% and rising by more than 0.1% in one month) signals an imminent monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rise > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. The interaction is necessary: the effect is only strong when both conditions occur together.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS up > 0.5% and UNRATE down > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances where PAYEMS rises >0.5% and UNRATE falls >0.2pp, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion phase, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening demand and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
evidence_refs: fact:late-cycle expansion typically associated with housing slowdowns
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when HOUST declines, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 (index 2017=100) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 90.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 220.0 (index 1982-1984=100) signals accelerating inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 220.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer spending (RSAFS) above 350,000 million dollars indicates strong household demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 350,000, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals robust aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. The effect is only significant when both indicators move positively together.
candidate_trigger: HOUST up > 0.5% and RSAFS up > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS rise >0.5%, or the interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05) in a 3-year rolling window.
